What this sprint means

Plain-language read of the numbers below. Every point links to the issues behind it.

    Burndown, with scope changes shown

    Work left to do each day against the plan. The orange line is total scope — when it rises, work was added mid-sprint. From the sprint’s record, not the filtered issues.

    Where each person's work sits

    Items per person, split by stage. Click any bar to see the issues.

    How long work takes, and how much of it is waiting

    Each closed item, from raised to done. The pale part is time spent waiting rather than being worked on.

    How long open work has been sitting

    Age of everything not yet done, in bands that match a two-week sprint.

    How long finished work took

    Every closed item, by the day it finished. The lines are what 50%, 85% and 95% of them came in under.

    Work in progress, and how old it is

    Open work against the same lines. Anything above them is already late, before it is late.

    How much finishes each week

    The series the forecast samples from. Quiet weeks are part of it, not gaps in it.

    Where the work has been sitting

    Cumulative flow. The height of the middle band is work in progress; the gap between the top two lines is the queue.

    Can we trust the forecast?

    Committed against completed, sprint by sprint. Consistency matters more than volume. From the sprint’s record, not the filtered issues.

    Monte Carlo forecast

    Run by the same tool the agent uses, over this team's whole recorded history. Follows the project, board and sprint selected above.

    Release quality & speed

    Four measures of how safely the team ships. From the release record, not the filtered issues.

    Team load

    Started-but-unfinished work, and how much arrived after planning. Both from issue status — no hours, no timesheets. From the sprint’s record, not the filtered issues.

    Business value delivered

    Estimated, not booked. Only items with a stated basis are counted.

    Releases & milestones

    Scope completion against target dates. From the release record, not the filtered issues.

    Who receives this board’s brief

    Sent by Jira’s own notifications, so nothing leaves your site. Recipients are Jira accounts and groups — never email addresses. Only a project administrator can change this.

    Risks and what to do about them

    Generated from the data on this page, not typed by hand. Each links to its issues.
